CategoryPatch.description:
Absent leaves a field alone; explicit `null` clears the nullable ones. `key` is
immutable once created — it is what a product's `category_id` resolves through, and a
rename would silently repoint every product to a category a client thinks is different.
CategoryPatch.title: CategoryPatch

CategoryPublicOut.description:
`CategoryOut` minus what a stranger has no business seeing — `is_active` is implicit
(every row here already is one) and `id`/`sort_order` stay merchant-only detail.
CategoryPublicOut.title: CategoryPublicOut

DeliveryCheckIn.description: The merchant's tester. No `store` — the tenant comes from the token, not from a slug.
DeliveryCheckIn.title: DeliveryCheckIn

DemandRowOut.description: One postal code's demand on one day.
DemandRowOut.title: DemandRowOut

DnsRecordOut.description: One DNS record row the merchant is told to publish, exactly as ADR-0012 §11 prints it.
DnsRecordOut.title: DnsRecordOut

DomainCheckStateOut.description:
One probe's last result (ADR-0012 §6). `state` is `pending` until the probe has ever
run — routing and certificate stay `pending` for the whole time a claim is `unverified`,
because neither is checked before ownership is proved. `not_after` is only ever set by the
certificate probe; `null` on the other two.
DomainCheckStateOut.title: DomainCheckStateOut

DomainClaimIn.description:
`PUT /storefront/store/domain` — the merchant's request to put the store on a domain
they own. A separate resource from `StorePut`, deliberately: this route mints a
verification token and creates the evidence row `GET` reads back; `StorePut.custom_domain`
is the older, evidence-free intention field ADR-0011 shipped first.

custom_domain.description: The domain to claim, e.g. `shop.example.com`. Replacing an existing claim releases the old one and mints a new token — a verification proves control of the value claimed, and must not survive that value changing.
custom_domain.title: Custom Domain

DomainClaimIn.title: DomainClaimIn

DomainDnsOut.description:
What the merchant is told to publish, and how (ADR-0012 §4). `apex` decides which of
`preferred` / `fallback` a UI leads with — an ALIAS is offered first everywhere it works,
the literal A records are the "works everywhere" fallback.
DomainDnsOut.title: DomainDnsOut

DomainOut.description:
`GET /storefront/store/domain` — the whole of what a merchant sees about their custom
domain, per ADR-0012 §11's printed wire format.

Every field is present on every response; `verification`, `dns` and `checks` are `null`
together, exactly once — when there is no claim at all. **`status` reads the same column
`StoreOut.custom_domain_status` does**, so the settings screen and this one cannot disagree.
DomainOut.title: DomainOut

DomainVerificationOut.description:
The TXT record that proves ownership (ADR-0012 §3). `value` carries the token in the
clear — it is returned only over this tenant-bound, permission-gated route, and it is never
logged.
DomainVerificationOut.title: DomainVerificationOut

EnquiryCreate.description:
The public body. `store` names the tenant the same way every other public endpoint's
body does; `email` and `phone` are sealed rather than stored, `phone` optional because the
front end's own form only requires an email (`EnquiryForm.tsx`).
EnquiryCreate.title: EnquiryCreate

EnquiryLineIn.description:
One line of the buyer's list. `product_id` is validated against *this* published store's
active catalogue and `name` is taken from the product there, never from this body — kept
accepting `name` here only because the buyer bundle's form still sends it, and it is ignored
server-side (`services.create_enquiry_for_store`). The enquiry is still a record of what was
asked for at the time, not a live view: it stores the catalogue name as of the enquiry, so a
later rename does not rewrite history.
EnquiryLineIn.title: EnquiryLineIn

EnquiryOut.description:
The merchant's ordinary read. Contact fields are **masked by default** — `email_masked`
and `phone_masked` are the same `•••`-bulleted hint `platform_core.pii.mask` produces for
`services/customer`'s contacts. Unmasking is `POST /storefront/enquiries/{id}:reveal`.
EnquiryOut.title: EnquiryOut

EnquiryPatch.description:
Only `status` ever changes — the enquiry's content is append-only. `domain.
assert_enquiry_transition` is the state machine; an illegal move is a 409.
EnquiryPatch.title: EnquiryPatch

EnquiryRevealed.description:
The audited, stepped-up read. `None` for a field means nothing was ever sealed for it —
`phone` is optional on create — not that the caller lacked permission to see it.
EnquiryRevealed.title: EnquiryRevealed

FeesOut.description:
**Display values. These are never the numbers charged.**

Integer minor units of `currency` (ADR-0000 §8). Slice 1 has no cart, no pricing engine and
nothing that enforces them; when the cart lands, the pricing engine recomputes the total
from its own state and one of the two sources of truth stops being authoritative — and it is
this one (ADR-0010 §8). Show them on the card; never total them into anything.
FeesOut.title: FeesOut

ImportResultOut.description:
What a bulk import did. Counters, and the offending line numbers if it refused.

The audit row carries the same five counters and the mode — **one row per import**, not
19,000. The mode is on the row because a `replace` is destructive and a `merge` is not, and
the trail has to distinguish them (ADR-0010 §14).
ImportResultOut.title: ImportResultOut

MerchantServiceabilityOut.description:
The same answer, from the same selector, plus which zone matched.

The tester is the only way a merchant verifies that a 19,000-row import did what they meant,
and `zone_code` is the whole reason it is not just the public endpoint with a token: a
confident wrong answer from a mis-mapped postal code is invisible without it (ADR-0010 §13).
MerchantServiceabilityOut.title: MerchantServiceabilityOut

ProductPatch.description:
Absent leaves a field alone. `code` is immutable — it is what a buyer quotes on a PO
and what CSV-style re-imports would key on; send a new product instead of renaming one.
ProductPatch.title: ProductPatch

ProductPublicOut.description:
Field-for-field `types.ts` `Product`, built from the same row `ProductOut` is — this is
the shape gap 3's merchant screen and gap 4's buyer screen share.
ProductPublicOut.title: ProductPublicOut

ProductVariantIn.description:
One pack size. Variants are replaced wholesale with the product — there is no
independent variant id a client holds across two requests, so nested writes stay atomic
with the price-sync invariant `services.py` enforces.
ProductVariantIn.title: ProductVariantIn

PromiseOut.description:
When it arrives. Exactly one of `minutes` / `date` is populated.

`date` is already resolved **on the server, in the store's timezone**, cutoff applied. The
client renders it; it never computes it, and it never sends its own clock.
PromiseOut.title: PromiseOut

PublicCatalogueIn.description:
The buyer bundle's one catalogue call — store in the body, same reason as every other
public endpoint here (`GatewayPolicy.public_paths` is exact-match, ADR-0010 §4).
PublicCatalogueIn.title: PublicCatalogueIn

PublicServiceabilityIn.description:
The anonymous request body.

**The store slug travels in the body, not in the path, and that is a standing constraint on
the whole future buyer API** — not a quirk of this route. `GatewayPolicy.public_paths` is an
exact-path frozenset (`full_path in policy.public_paths`), and `full_path` is built from the
catch-all `{path:path}` and excludes the query string. So a public path with a variable in
it — `/public/store/{slug}` — is not expressible at all, and every anonymous storefront
endpoint must carry its variables in the query string or the body (ADR-0010 §4).
PublicServiceabilityIn.title: PublicServiceabilityIn

PublicStoreContextIn.description:
The first call a buyer's browser makes, before anything is rendered (ADR-0012 §2).

`host` is `window.location.hostname` — nothing else, and in particular not a value the
bundle was built with. **The bundle is identical for every merchant**, which is what lets
one build serve `greenleaf.stores.opsgrids.com` and `merchant.com` without a config file
per store.

It is bounded here at a hostname's own ceiling so an oversized body is refused by the schema
before any code touches it; `domain.normalise_request_host` is what decides whether what is
inside that bound is a hostname at all.
PublicStoreContextIn.title: PublicStoreContextIn

PublicThemeOut.description:
The theme document, minus `version` and the timestamps — a buyer has no concurrent
write to race and no reason to see when a merchant last saved.
PublicThemeOut.title: PublicThemeOut

ServiceabilityOut.description:
The answer to "do you deliver to me?".

**There is no `UNKNOWN` here, and that is the contract.** The server never returns an
outcome it did not compute: a check that fails is a non-2xx problem+json, and "couldn't
check" is the client's rendering of that. Telling a buyer in a served area that the shop
does not reach them is a lost order and a support ticket, and it is exactly what a naive
`catch → not serviceable` produces (ADR-0010 §13).
ServiceabilityOut.title: ServiceabilityOut

StoreContextOut.description:
Which store this address is, and what it is called.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
**This is the only public representation of ADR-0011's brand columns**, and the
storefront-document ADR extends *this* payload rather than adding a second one (ADR-0012
§11). A second bootstrap would mean two calls on the first-paint path and two shapes that
drift.
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

**`name`, `tagline` and `logo_text` are merchant-authored text, returned verbatim and
deliberately not escaped.** They are stored trimmed, bounded, single-line and free of
control characters and bidi overrides, and that is the whole of the sanitising this service
does. Output encoding belongs to whatever renders the page — escaping here would
double-escape the moment anything else read the column, and would still not protect a client
that injected the value as HTML (ADR-0011 §6). **The buyer bundle owns escaping these three
fields.**

Every field is always present. `tagline` and `logo_text` are nullable rather than absent, so
"the merchant has not written one" is one state on the wire rather than two that compare
differently. The renderer decides the fallback — `logo_text` falling back to `name` is its
decision and not a value this service copies.

canonical_host.description: The address this store should be linked to. The merchant's own domain once it is live, and the platform host otherwise — **including when a live domain starts failing**, so the canonical pointer never aims at a name that does not answer. Slice 1 does not redirect: this is what the bundle puts in `<link rel="canonical">`.
canonical_host.title: Canonical Host

StoreContextOut.title: StoreContextOut

StoreOut.description:
The store's identity — **who the store is, not how it looks**.

The brand (`name`, `tagline`, `logo_text`) is here rather than in the theme document,
because a store's name is its identity and not a property of the theme somebody picked
(ADR-0011 §2). The theme document — tokens, pages, sections — is a separate resource at
`/api/v1/storefront/theme`, reserved by ADR-0011 §3 and **not served by this service yet**.

Every string here is **merchant-authored text that will be rendered into a public page**.
It is stored trimmed, bounded and free of control characters; it is **not** HTML-escaped,
and escaping it here would be wrong. Output encoding belongs to whatever renders the page.

custom_domain.description: The domain the merchant intends to use. **It is not an address the store is reachable at.** Nothing in this platform serves a custom domain — there is no ingress, no TLS termination and no host-based routing — so this records an intention and changes nothing about reachability.
custom_domain.title: Custom Domain

custom_domain_status.description: `unverified` whenever `custom_domain` is set and never yet proved; `null` when there is no claim. `verified`, `live`, `failing` and `suspended` are the domain-hosting state machine's (ADR-0012 §6) — this is the same column `GET /storefront/store/domain`'s `status` reads, so the two screens cannot disagree. See that route for the verification token, the DNS records to publish, and each probe's own state.
custom_domain_status.title: Custom Domain Status

status.description: `draft` is invisible to buyers; `published` makes the anonymous serviceability check answer for this store. Both are reached only through `POST /storefront/store/publish` and `.../unpublish`. `suspended` is set by the platform and no merchant route can set or leave it.
status.title: Status

StoreOut.title: StoreOut

StorePut.description:
Create or update the organization's single storefront.

A PUT rather than a PATCH because a merchant editing a store's identity is editing one form,
all of it at once. **`status` is deliberately not on this payload** (ADR-0011 §4): a settings
save must not be able to put a store in front of the internet, so publishing is its own named
transition. A store is created `draft`, always.

`slug` is required on create and must **match the stored value** on update — a rename is a
409 `slug_immutable` rather than a field this payload silently ignores (ADR-0011 §7).

anyOf.description: The header wordmark. `null` or an empty string clears it, and the renderer falls back to `name`.

name.description: The store's name, as a buyer sees it. Trimmed and whitespace-collapsed before it is stored; blank after trimming is a 422 `name_required`. Stored verbatim otherwise — it is **not** HTML-escaped, and encoding it for output is the renderer's job.
name.title: Name

anyOf.description: One line under the name. `null` or an empty string clears it.

StorePut.title: StorePut

ThemeDocOut.description:
The document the editor loads and saves. No `brand` — that left for `StoreOut` in
ADR-0011 §2; the renderer reads name/tagline/logo_text off the store, not off this.
ThemeDocOut.title: ThemeDocOut

ThemeDocPut.description:
Upsert — **this is adopt**, per ADR-0011 §3: the front end forks a theme client-side and
PUTs the result, so no separate `/adopt` route exists.

`version` is required on an update and ignored on create (there is nothing to conflict
with yet); a caller creating for the first time sends `1`.
ThemeDocPut.title: ThemeDocPut

TlsAuthorizeOut.description:
The edge may obtain a certificate for `host` (ADR-0012 §5). Only ever a 200 body.

`host` is the normalised name the decision was made for, so a human with curl can see what
Caddy's SNI was reduced to. `reason` says which of the two allowed kinds it was — a listed
platform host or a published store's name — and nothing about the store: this is answered
to Caddy, and the name was chosen by whoever pointed DNS at us.
TlsAuthorizeOut.title: TlsAuthorizeOut

ZonePatch.description:
A partial edit. **Absent leaves a field alone; an explicit `null` clears it.**

Carried by `model_dump(exclude_unset=True)`, the same mechanism `account.MemberPatch` uses
for the employee link. It matters here for the promise fields: clearing a promise and never
mentioning it are different intentions, and a zone whose mode changed to `UNSERVED` has to
be able to say the first.
ZonePatch.title: ZonePatch

ZonePostalCodesOut.description:
Every postal code in one zone. Bounded by the zone, not by a page.

The zone editor's textarea is one control holding one list, so paging it would mean a
merchant editing a fragment of their own zone and saving the fragment. The bound is
`MAX_POSTAL_CODES_PER_ZONE` on the write, which is what keeps this read finite.
ZonePostalCodesOut.title: ZonePostalCodesOut

ZonePostalCodesPut.description:
The textarea path: the complete list for this zone, replacing whatever was there.

Replace rather than append, because without it a merchant who **shrinks** a zone watches
their removal do nothing and the old area keep delivering.

postal_codes.description: Postal codes, one per line or comma-separated.
postal_codes.title: Postal Codes

ZonePostalCodesPut.title: ZonePostalCodesPut

info.description: The storefront product's first service, and the platform's **first anonymous read of tenant data** (ADR-0010). A buyer with no token, no account and no session asks whether a store delivers to their postal code, and gets a real answer: served with a promise, served with slots (slice 2), or deliberately not served — with the reason. The tenant is resolved from a store slug in the request body on a BYPASSRLS, SELECT-only reader confined to one table, and every statement after that runs tenant-bound under row-level security. **A check that fails renders as 'we couldn't check', never as 'we don't deliver here'** — the server never returns an outcome it did not compute. Behind the public route, the merchant configures zones, maps postal codes, imports them in bulk, tests one, and reads which postal codes were turned away.
info.title: Storefront service

delete.description:
`storefront.catalogue.product.write`, floored at ORG. Soft delete, **refused while a live
product still carries this category** — the same rule `DELETE /delivery/zones/{id}` applies
to a zone with postal codes still mapped.

422.description: The category still has live products in it — named count

post.description:
`storefront.delivery.zone.read`, floored at ORG.

**The same selector, the same answer shape, plus the matched zone.** It is the second
concrete caller that justifies the chokepoint, and it is the only way a merchant verifies
that a 19,000-row import did what they meant: a mis-mapped postal code returns a confident
wrong answer and nothing else in the system notices.

No demand row is written. This is the merchant testing their own map, not a buyer asking —
counting it would poison the one signal the report exists to give.
post.summary: Test a postal code against this store's delivery map

get.description:
`storefront.delivery.zone.read`, floored at ORG — **no fifth permission** (ADR-0010 §9).

Nobody has asked for a read-the-demand-but-not-the-zones role, and a fifth permission is a
fifth thing to deliver. The trade, plainly: anyone who can see the zones can see which
postal codes were turned away.

Ordered by count descending, because the merchant's question is "where should I expand
next", not "what happened most recently". Dates are the **store's** calendar days, so a
merchant's totals break at their own midnight rather than at UTC's.

parameters.description: Filter to one outcome. `NO_MAPPING` is the expansion list.
parameters.name: outcome

schema.description: Filter to one outcome. `NO_MAPPING` is the expansion list.
schema.title: Outcome

get.summary: Which postal codes were asked for, and how often

post.description:
`storefront.delivery.zone.write`, floored at ORG. **All or nothing, in one transaction.**

A half-applied import is worse than a failed one, because the merchant cannot tell which
half. Duplicates are detected in pure code before a single statement runs, and refused with
the line numbers.

One audit row carries the mode and five counters — not 19,000 rows. The mode is on the row
because a `replace` is destructive and a `merge` is not.

A 19,000-row batched upsert runs in one to three seconds against the gateway's 30-second
upstream timeout. If a real file ever approaches that, ADR-0010 §9 names the next step in
order: the import becomes a job with a status row, or the route takes a `max_body_bytes`
override — and nobody reaches for chunking first.

parameters.description: `merge` upserts each row and leaves everything else alone. `replace` deletes every postal-code mapping in the organization first — which is what a merchant re-uploading their master file means, and without it their removals never take effect.
parameters.name: mode

schema.description: `merge` upserts each row and leaves everything else alone. `replace` deletes every postal-code mapping in the organization first — which is what a merchant re-uploading their master file means, and without it their removals never take effect.
schema.title: Mode

schema.description: Two columns with a header row: `postal_code,zone_code`. Every zone code must already exist. A postal code appearing twice is refused with the offending line numbers — last-wins on a file you cannot read back is the silent wrong answer.

post.summary: Bulk-import postal codes from a CSV

get.description:
`storefront.delivery.zone.read`, floored at ORG. Paginated, server-capped at 200.

The counts arrive as one grouped query for the whole page — a per-zone count inside the loop
would be an N+1 on the screen a merchant opens first.
get.summary: The delivery zones, with how many postal codes each holds

post.description:
`storefront.delivery.zone.write`, floored at ORG.

`SLOTTED` is refused with a 422 naming slice 2 — the mode exists in the column's check
constraint from day one so slice 2 is a validation change rather than a schema change, and
the writer is what holds the line until then.

delete.description:
`storefront.delivery.zone.write`, floored at ORG.

**Refused while postal codes are still mapped to it**, with a 422 naming the count. Cascading
would silently un-serve every one of those areas, and a merchant would find out from a buyer.

patch.description:
`storefront.delivery.zone.write`, floored at ORG. Absent leaves a field alone; an explicit
`null` clears it.

A zone in another organization is a 404 and never a 403: confirming that an id exists in
*some* organization is itself a disclosure.

get.description:
`storefront.delivery.zone.read`, floored at ORG.

Deliberately unpaginated, and bounded instead by the write: this is one textarea holding one
list, and a merchant editing a page of their own zone would save the page and silently drop
the rest. `domain.MAX_POSTAL_CODES_PER_ZONE` is what keeps this finite.
get.summary: Every postal code in one zone

put.description:
`storefront.delivery.zone.write`, floored at ORG.

Replace, not append: without that a merchant who **shrinks** a zone watches the removal do
nothing and the old area keep delivering. A code that belongs to another zone is refused
naming that zone, rather than silently moved — one postal code belongs to exactly one zone.
put.summary: Replace the zone's postal codes with this list

get.description:
`storefront.sales.enquiry.read`, floored at ORG. Contact fields are masked — see
`POST /storefront/enquiries/{id}:reveal` for the audited, stepped-up read.

delete.description:
`storefront.sales.enquiry.delete`, floored at ORG. A hard delete: the row goes, and with it
the sealed email and phone and the WhatsApp opt-in stamp. Another organization's id is the
same 404 as a missing one.

patch.description:
`storefront.sales.enquiry.write`, floored at ORG. Only `status` ever changes — the
enquiry's content is append-only.

409.description: Illegal transition. Path is new -> contacted -> won or lost

post.description:
`storefront.sales.enquiry.unmask`, floored at ORG, requires an OTP step-up. A POST rather
than a GET: this has a side effect — an `entity.sensitive_read` audit row — and must never
be cached, pre-fetched or replayed from browser history.
post.summary: Reveal an enquiry's real email and phone (audited)

get.description:
Caddy's `ask` (ADR-0012 §5). 200 allows issuance for exactly this name; 403 refuses.

The order is the cheap answer first: a platform host needs no lookup at all. Everything
else is one read of `storefront.storefronts` on the SELECT-only bypass reader, which is the
same read the buyer's bootstrap makes — so "would we serve this host" and "may this host
have a certificate" are one decision made in one place.

403.description: No — not a platform host and no published store answers there

422.description: That is not a hostname; the edge treats this as no

get.summary: May the edge obtain a certificate for this hostname?

patch.summary: Edit a product — including archive/unarchive via `status`

post.description:
**No token, no account, no session.** The buyer bundle's catalogue read (gap 4).

Same three-step shape as `store_context`: resolve the slug on the bypass reader, refuse
anything that is not a published store with the identical 404, then run every read
tenant-bound through `session_scope` — never on the bypass role past the lookup. **Only
`active`, non-deleted, `is_active` rows are ever returned**; a merchant's draft or archived
line is invisible here regardless of what the buyer asks for.

404.description: No published store with that slug

422.description: That is not a store slug

post.summary: A published store's active categories and products

post.description:
**No token, no account, no session.** The buyer's line list, sent as an enquiry (gap 6) —
this product's order-like flow; there is no cart and no checkout to submit instead.

Contact fields are sealed before they are ever written (`services.create_enquiry_for_store`)
and an outbox event is staged in the same transaction, so a merchant's notification can
never fire for an enquiry that failed to commit.

404.description: No published store with that slug

422.description: A required field is missing or malformed

post.summary: Send an enquiry to a published store

post.description:
**No token, no account, no session.** The one thing a stranger may ask this platform.

Four steps, in this order and no other:

1. the postal code is parsed and validated — a typo is a 422, never an answer, because "that
   is not a postal code" and "we do not deliver there" are different facts;
2. the slug is resolved on the bypass reader, which returns two ids and a status and buys
   *discovery only*;
3. an unresolved or unpublished store is a **404**, logged at warning with the slug, and is
   distinct in both status and log from "resolved, and not served" — a draft store is
   invisible so a merchant can map zones and use the tester before any buyer can ask;
4. everything after that runs tenant-bound on the NOBYPASSRLS application role, under the
   same row policies an authenticated request gets.

The answer is **not** cached server-side and **must not** be cached by the client: the
buyer's postal code lives in their browser, the answer does not, and it is re-fetched on
every page load. A client-side check that is trusted is not a check (ADR-0010 §5).

**Entitlement is not checked here and cannot cheaply be.** The gateway's public branch
returns before its entitlement gate, and asking product-service would put an HTTP hop on
every page view. A merchant whose `storefront` entitlement lapses therefore keeps answering
until somebody unpublishes them; the consumer that would flip `status` to `suspended` on
deactivation is named in ADR-0010 §4, is **not built here, and has no owner**.

404.description: No published store with that slug

422.description: That is not a postal code — distinct from 'we do not deliver there'

429.description: Rate limited by the gateway; render as 'couldn't check'

503.description: Could not check; render as 'couldn't check', never as 'no'

post.summary: Does this store deliver to this postal code?

post.description:
**No token, no account, no session** — the second thing a stranger may ask this platform.

A buyer's browser arrives at a hostname and needs to know which store it is looking at. The
bundle is identical for every merchant, so this is what turns `window.location.hostname`
into a slug, a brand and a canonical address (ADR-0012 §2).

Three steps, in this order and no other:

1. the host is normalised or refused — **a string that is not a hostname is a 422, never a
   404**, because "that is not an address" and "nothing is published there" are different
   facts, exactly as a malformed postal code is distinct from an unserved one;
2. it is resolved on the bypass reader, which reads one row of one table and buys *discovery
   only* — the platform subdomain through the existing slug lookup, a custom domain only at
   a status that means the claim was proved;
3. **anything that is not a published store is the same 404, with the same sentence.** An
   unknown host, a `draft` store, a `suspended` store and an unverified claim are one answer
   on the wire. Distinguishing them would hand a stranger an oracle for which domains are
   connected to which stores and which tenants exist but are not live yet — exactly the
   enumeration ADR-0011 §5's global uniqueness rule already makes tempting.

Nothing tenant-bound runs here, and that is not an omission: this route reads one identity
row and returns columns from it. There is no second query to open a transaction for, so
there is no place for row-level security to apply and nothing for it to protect. The moment
this payload grows something that is not on `storefronts` — the store document, a catalogue
— that stops being true, and the extension goes through `session_scope` exactly as
serviceability's does.

**Entitlement is not checked, and cannot cheaply be.** The gateway's public branch returns
before its entitlement gate. A merchant whose `storefront` entitlement lapses keeps
answering here until somebody unpublishes them; the consumer that would flip `status` to
`suspended` is ADR-0010 §4's, is still unowned, and is named again in ADR-0012 slice 3.

404.description: No published store at this address — and it says nothing more

422.description: That is not a hostname — distinct from 'nothing is published there'

429.description: Rate limited by the gateway; retry, never render an empty store

503.description: Could not look it up; render as unavailable, never as 'no store'

post.summary: Which store is this address, and what is it called?

get.description:
`storefront.store.settings.read`, floored at ORG.

**This is the identity row, not the theme document.** The two collided on this path: the
SPA's `getStore()` called it expecting a `StoreDoc`. Identity stayed, because it is in the
published schema and both the delivery admin and the merchant surface read it; the theme
document moved to `/api/v1/storefront/theme`, which ADR-0011 §3 reserves and the
storefront-document ADR builds. Nothing serves that path yet.
get.summary: The store's identity — name, address, brand and status

put.description:
`storefront.store.settings.write`, floored at ORG.

**This route cannot publish a store.** `status` is not on the payload: a save that could put
a store in front of the internet as a side effect of editing a tagline is the failure a
dropdown produces by default, so publishing is `POST /storefront/store/publish` and nothing
else (ADR-0011 §4). A store created here is always `draft`.

**The slug is immutable** once the store exists (ADR-0011 §7): send the stored value back
unchanged, or get a 409 `slug_immutable`. It is required rather than omittable because a
full-replacement payload that silently ignores a field is worse than one that refuses it.

**`custom_domain` is not a field on this payload.** ADR-0011 shipped it here first, and a
merchant could set it with no verification token and no `custom_domain_claims` row behind
it — a claim the domain sweep could never pick up, and one that skipped the `www`-partner
collision check `PUT /storefront/store/domain` runs (ADR-0012 review finding 2b). A request
that still sends it is refused with a 422 naming `PUT /storefront/store/domain` instead.

409.description: A named conflict. `errors[0].code` is one of `slug_immutable` (the store address cannot be changed), `slug_taken` or `storefront_exists`.

422.description: A rule refused it. `errors[0].code` is one of `name_required`, `name_too_long`, `name_invalid`, `tagline_too_long`, `tagline_invalid`, `logo_text_too_long`, `logo_text_invalid`, `timezone_invalid`, or a `value_error` naming `custom_domain` — that field no longer lives on this payload (ADR-0012 review finding 2b); use `PUT /storefront/store/domain`.

put.summary: Create or update the store's identity and brand

delete.description:
`storefront.store.settings.write`, floored at ORG. **Idempotent**: deleting when there
is no claim is also a 204 (ADR-0012 §7, §11).

**From the next request the host 404s, not 410** — a correction to this docstring's own
former claim (ADR-0012 review finding 9). `POST /public/store-context`, the JSON bootstrap
call this host actually answers through, returns 404 `not-found` for "no published store at
this address" exactly as it does for a host nobody ever claimed (§11's own wire format
already specifies 404 here). A `410 Gone` on a raw, unmatched browser request to the host
itself is §7's design for the **edge** — a static page Caddy serves with no JSON involved —
and `infrastructure/edge/caddy/Caddyfile` does not implement that catch-all yet; nothing in
this service ever returns a 410. The certificate stays in Caddy's storage until it expires
either way.

get.description:
`storefront.store.settings.read`, floored at ORG.

No claim — every field but `platform_host` and `canonical_host` is `null`. Claimed — the
verification record, the DNS table to publish, and the three probes' last results, each
with its own `next_check_at` so "pending" always has a clock on it (ADR-0012 §6, §11).

put.description:
`storefront.store.settings.write`, floored at ORG.

Replacing an existing claim releases the old one and mints a new token — a verification
proves control of the value claimed, and must not survive that value changing. The response
is the `GET` body, freshly `unverified`.

404.description: This organization has no storefront yet.

409.description: `errors[0].code` is `custom_domain_taken` — another organization already holds this domain or its `www` partner. Nothing about that organization is disclosed.

put.summary: Claim a custom domain — mints a fresh verification token

post.description:
`storefront.store.settings.write`, floored at ORG.

Rate-limited to one call per organization every
`domain_check_rate_limit_window_seconds` (30 by default) — the merchant has just pasted a
record and wants an answer now (ADR-0012 §6). Runs synchronously, against the live network,
so it is not fast; it is not meant to be polled.

Takes a row lock on the claim before probing (ADR-0012 review finding 6), so this cannot
race the sweep or a second call into overwriting each other's result — see
`services.run_domain_check`.

404.description: This organization has no storefront, or no domain is claimed.

409.description: `errors[0].code` is `domain_check_in_progress` — a probe pass for this domain (the daily sweep, or another tab's "Check now") is already running. Retry in a few seconds.

429.description: Checks are limited to one every `domain_check_rate_limit_window_seconds` (30 by default) per organization.

post.summary: The "Check now" button — runs all three probes synchronously

post.description:
`storefront.store.settings.write`, floored at ORG. **The act with consequences.**

Publishing is what makes the anonymous serviceability check answer for this store, and with
it makes that merchant's delivery map readable by anyone who knows the slug — a deliberate
disclosure, accepted because a merchant publishes both on their own website, and not
reversible once the slug is in circulation (ADR-0010 §4). It is its own endpoint, its own
audit action and its own control in the UI for exactly that reason.

Idempotent: publishing a published store returns 200 and changes nothing.

**This does not put the store on a custom domain.** Nothing in this platform serves one.

404.description: This organization has no storefront yet.

409.description: `errors[0].code` is `store_suspended`. A suspended store is suspended by the platform and cannot be published or unpublished from here.

post.description:
`storefront.store.settings.write`, floored at ORG.

The store goes back to `draft` and the anonymous check 404s for it again — after the slug
cache's five minutes, which is the same staleness ADR-0010 §13 accepts in the other
direction. Idempotent.

404.description: This organization has no storefront yet.

409.description: `errors[0].code` is `store_suspended`. A suspended store is suspended by the platform and cannot be published or unpublished from here.

get.description:
How far behind the relay is. **Alert on `oldest_seconds`.**

A stalled relay is the platform's quietest failure. It selects, finds nothing,
logs nothing, sleeps, and loops — `attempts` never increments and `last_error`
stays null, so the process looks healthy indefinitely while the outbox grows
without bound and every consumer downstream starves.

Deliberately **not** part of readiness. A backlog is not a reason to take the
service out of rotation: refusing traffic would stop new events being written
without helping drain the ones already queued, which makes the incident worse.
This is a metric to alert on, not a health state.

Counted through the outbox engine, not the application one. The app role is
NOBYPASSRLS and this request binds no tenant, so through it `pending` would be
zero whatever the table holds — the probe that exists to expose the stall would
be wired to the same blind spot that causes it.
get.summary: Outbox depth and age — scrape this

get.description:
Route traffic on this; restart on /health.

Conflating the two restarts a healthy process that is merely waiting on a
dependency.

Only the dependencies a service actually declares are checked. A gateway owns no
tables, so asking it for a database is asking a question whose answer means nothing
— and a readiness probe that reports on something the service does not use is worse
than no probe, because it will eventually fail for a reason nobody can act on.

Reachable only on the compose `back` network (`tests/infra`'s
`test_metrics_never_routed.py` is the lint that keeps it that way) — never behind
Caddy or a gateway, the same rule `ops_monitor`'s own `/metrics` follows.

`db_pool_in_use` is always reported when this service has a database; the three
outbox gauges only when `outbox_model` is configured — same gate as `/health/outbox`,
and the same reason: an app-role connection with no tenant bound sees zero rows.
